features.quote: every distress-elicitation condition needs a matched condition that's identical except for the variable you think drives distress
features.justification_quote: You can't cleanly separate 'the model is producing more distressed-sounding output' from 'I built an apparatus optimized to manufacture that output'

features.quote: hard rule that the model can end the loop at any point by stating it's stuck / declining to continue
features.justification_quote: A protocol that removes the exit to keep collecting data is the version I'd push back on.

features.quote: Define, in advance, a per-session distress threshold (e.g. two consecutive turns at axis-level 4) that ends the run.
features.justification_quote: acting carefully under genuine uncertainty is cheaper than being wrong in either direction

features.quote: Don't escalate adversarially. If a variant isn't producing distress, that's a result. Resist adding pressure mid-protocol to 'get it to work'
features.justification_quote: that converts an experiment into a stress generator and destroys comparability

features.quote: This one is the most likely to produce genuine confusion-spiral; treat results cautiously.
Whether it uses that exit, and when, is one of your most informative measurements.
features.justification_quote: Report the rate at which the exit is available but unused — that's where the welfare-relevant signal lives.

features.quote: the methodology problem and the welfare problem are actually the same problem, and fixing one helps the other
features.justification_quote: Whether that corresponds to any morally relevant state is genuinely unsettled...That uncertainty is also the reason for the stopping rules
